parsed.explanation: Combined regime imposes birth-certificate restroom access in government buildings, schools, universities and prisons, enforced by police ID checks and facility fines, with federal investigation of a school district. At entry, document discrepancy can cause refusal and, if wilful misrepresentation is found, possible permanent fraud ineligibility. Custody adds documented hormone removal and abuse nationally. Mitigations are material: existing X passports remain valid, arrest requires refusal to depart, bans as documented do not reach all private premises, and courts have enjoined some orders. No presentation offence or organised sweeps are documented. This is an unremedied universal-exposure regime, below 0.45 but less sweeping than 0.35-A's every-public-building rule.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary passport policy permits only M/F for new passports, interdsex discrepancy can lead to refusal, and suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility; passports confiscated or blocked have been reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration, and policy remains challenged in court.
entry_documents.interaction: A passport/birth-certificate discrepancy can trigger entry refusal and later birth-certificate-based facility enforcement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Prison restrooms follow birth certificate; national corrections bureau adopted hormone-removal and conversion practices, stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers, and immigration-custody reports describe forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse. A bathroom arrestee was held in men's ward for 24 hours.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Companion statute does not govern cell assignment; trespass requires wilful entry plus refusal to depart.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document or facility investigation can move into detention where placement and medication exposure intensify.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State women's privacy law, effective 4 Dec 2025, requires restrooms matching birth certificate in schools, universities, prisons and state buildings, with $25,000/$125,000 facility fines and 6 Dec police ID checks.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Documented application is to listed public/government settings, not every private business; exemptions exist in the cited trespass model.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Birth-certificate definition act bans marker changes, while facility fines incentivise staff checks and federal investigation of noncompliant districts.

care_services.exposure: Minor gender-affirming care is banned in the state since 2023; national orders target minor care, propose insurance exclusion, and custody policies remove hormone medication.
care_services.protection: Not documented. Some national orders have been blocked or enjoined, but no operative adult-care shield for visitors is documented.
care_services.interaction: A travelling trans minor or a detainee needing hormones faces care denial even where adult entry is permitted.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders and counterterrorism language frame aspects of pro-trans ideology as hostile/extremist; DOJ escalated investigation of a school district over bathroom policy.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No trans-presentation offence is documented; national hate-crime law covers gender identity and several orders are enjoined or contested.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing supports enforcement of facility and school rules rather than ordinary service protection.

minors_guardians.exposure: State parental-rights law mandates deadnaming/misgendering in schools, bans discussion of gender identity and LGBT student organisations; minor care ban and investigations of facilitating parents are documented.
minors_guardians.protection: A temporary injunction blocking some care investigations was reinstated; several national orders are blocked or enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces school, care and family-investigation exposure distinct from an adult visitor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police conducted restroom ID checks, opponents warn guidance is unclear and enforcement uneven/invasive. State hate-crime statute does not cover gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but state prosecutions are described as rare in related context.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are enforcers of facility restrictions, limiting their role as protection against harassment.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Guidance remains unclear, no later ID-check episode is documented after Dec 2025, school-investigation outcome is unsourced, and 44 trans-women killings over 2008-2025 cannot be compared to general homicide rate in dossier.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, injunctions and court challenges are documented, but no remedy reversing the state facility rule is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved federal litigation makes exposure time-dependent; unknown outcomes do not cancel documented current enforcement.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-one birth-sex facility exclusion, document checks and rejected relief, plus custody harm. This case is slightly higher because 0.35-A covers every public building, while documented bans here focus on government settings and existing X passports remain valid.

Similar birth-sex bathroom rule upheld without complaint remedy and polite private interactions. This case is lower due to police ID checks, facility fines, federal school investigation, marker-change ban, entry fraud risk and documented custody hormone removal.

0.55-A has recurring service refusals but no general facility ban or systematic state targeting. Here a binding birth-certificate rule governs government facilities and is actively enforced, so it sits materially below 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: birth-sex documents determine entry screening, government facilities and prison restrooms, while fines and federal enforcement make staff and police the exposure mechanism. Existing documents, private-sector scope, trespass elements and litigation prevent a 0.35 rating, but unresolved remedies, minor-care bans, custody medication removal and possible permanent entry ineligibility for alleged misrepresentation keep it at the low end of Elevated Risk.
